findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 17 mm is observed in the tail of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. The tumor extends beyond the inferior border of the duodenum. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in one node at station 1 and four nodes at station 9. Osteolytic changes are noted on the left side of the Th8 vertebral body, suggesting bone metastasis.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU1 (invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the arterial branches)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the omentum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (17 mm) and the extent of local invasion, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the tail are:
- Station 1: left gastric artery
- Station 4: common hepatic artery
- Station 7: celiac artery
- Station 9: superior mesenteric artery
- Station 11: inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are:
- Station 1: 1 node
- Station 9: 4 nodes

The regional lymph nodes are stations 1 and 9. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within these regional stations, there are 5 nodes (1 node at station 1 and 4 nodes at station 9). Therefore, the N classification is N1b.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

The presence of osteolytic changes on the left side of the Th8 vertebral body suggests bone metastasis, which is a distant metastasis. Therefore, the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor has invaded the duodenum (DU1) and the omentum (OO1), which are criteria for Unresectable (UR). Therefore, the resectability classification is Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1b), and M (M1) categories, the overall stage is Stage IV.
